investigate: The study is the ==first empirical examination== of inquiry-based instruction in Austrian primary science classrooms.
It asks how far inquiry-based strategies are enacted, ==which instructional profiles teachers show==, and how these relate to professionalisation and gender.
Latent Class Analysis was applied to ==self-reports from 339 teachers== in the 2019 TIMSS teacher survey.
find: The analysis revealed ==four distinct instructional profiles==.
About two-thirds of teachers reported combining inquiry-based strategies, yet ==only one profile reflected a comprehensive inquiry approach==, with students engaged throughout the inquiry cycle.
Profile membership was ==significantly associated with gender and professional development==; the authors call for stronger reflective competencies in teacher education.

caption.question: How is inquiry-based teaching actually practised in primary science classrooms?
caption.intro: Doris Neubauer-Hametner, Heike Wendt and Daniel Kasper use 2019 TIMSS survey data from 339 Austrian teachers to identify **profiles of inquiry-based instructional strategies** in primary science.

source_notes.investigate: Abstract sentences 2-5: first empirical examination; aims (i)-(iii); secondary data from the 2019 TIMSS teacher survey in Austria (n teacher = 339); Latent Class Analysis of teachers' self-reports.
source_notes.find: Abstract sentences 6-10: four distinct profiles; about two-thirds combine strategies, only one profile comprehensive across the inquiry cycle; significant associations with gender and professional development (multinomial logistic regression); need to strengthen deep instructional structures and reflective competencies in initial teacher education and ongoing professional development. 'Call for' renders 'underscore the need'.
